extracted.intended_audience: operators of PHMSA‑regulated pipelines; pipeline safety/compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and compliance criteria for rupture‑mitigation valves (RMVs) and alternative equivalent technologies on onshore transmission pipelines, including installation, operation, monitoring, maintenance, notification, and recordkeeping obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: RMV/alternative shut‑off timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Following a 'notification of potential rupture,' an operator must identify whether a rupture is occurring and close RMVs and alternative equivalent technologies as soon as practicable, but no later than within 30 minutes of rupture identification, or, if applicable, no later than the shut‑down times used in calculating a worst‑case discharge in accordance with §194.105(b)(1), whichever is a shorter time interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must use the shorter of the 30‑minute standard or the pipeline's worst‑case discharge shut‑down time from part 194 calculations. Identification of rupture must precede valve closure; timing is measured from rupture identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve monitoring and control capability
rubrics_metrics.description: RMVs and alternative equivalent technologies must be capable of being monitored or controlled by remote or on‑site personnel, operated during all operating conditions, and monitored for valve status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators using remote‑control valves (RCVs) or ASVs must ensure monitoring/control capability. Exception: operators using automatic shut‑off valves (ASVs) as RMVs do not need remote monitoring of the valve itself if the operator can monitor pipeline pressures or product flow rate to identify and locate a rupture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual valve personnel designation and proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators using a manual valve as an alternative equivalent technology must appropriately designate and locate personnel near the valve to ensure valve shut‑off consistent with this section and RMV performance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When manual valves are used in lieu of RMVs, operators must demonstrate staffing and proximity arrangements sufficient to meet the shut‑off timing/performance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption requests for non‑HCA segments
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators of pipelines in non‑HCAs or of segments that could not affect an HCA may submit for PHMSA review, within a notification under §195.18 requesting installation of manual valves as an alternative equivalent technology, an exemption from the valve operation requirements of §195.419.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification must include the closing times for those manual valves for PHMSA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance, inspection, and operator drills requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must perform maintenance, inspection, and operator drills to ensure they can close an RMV or alternative equivalent technology as soon as practicable, but within 30 minutes following rupture identification or within their part 194 shut‑down times, whichever is shorter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHMSA finalizes initial validation drill requirements and periodic confirmation drills for manually or locally operated valves used as alternatives. Drills ensure operational capability; documentation of drill outcomes and follow‑up is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drill closure minimum threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: During required drills for manual or locally operated valves, operators are not required to fully close the valves; a closure of 25 percent, at a minimum, is sufficient to be compliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This minimum applies to compliance with drill execution — a partial closure (≥25%) during drill suffices to demonstrate capability for the purposes of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remediation timeline after failed drill
rubrics_metrics.description: If the 30‑minute maximum closure time (or shorter part 194 time) cannot be achieved during the drill, the operator must revise response efforts and repair any valves to achieve compliance as soon as practicable but no later than 12 months after the drill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators may request, via the §195.18 notification procedure, an extension of the 12‑month repair timeline if repair within 12 months would be economically, technically, or operationally infeasible (examples: prohibitive costs, access/permit issues, long procurement lead times, component/labor availability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim alternative measures after failed drill
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative valve shut‑off measures must be in place within 7 days of a failed drill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must implement interim measures to mitigate risk while repairs or longer‑term fixes proceed under the remediation timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point‑to‑point verification for RCVs
rubrics_metrics.description: For each remote‑control valve (RCV) installed under §§195.258(c) or 195.418, the operator must conduct a point‑to‑point verification between SCADA displays, the installed valves, sensors, and communications equipment in accordance with §195.446(c) and (e), or perform an equivalent verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification must confirm end‑to‑end integrity of monitoring and control communications and instrumentation supporting RCV operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share corrective actions and lessons learned network‑wide
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators are required to identify corrective actions and lessons learned resulting from validation and confirmation drills and share and implement them across the operator's entire network of pipeline systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drill findings must inform system‑wide improvements; documentation and dissemination across assets are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency flow restricting devices in HCAs must meet RMV requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency flow restriction devices installed as preventive/mitigative measures in HCAs must meet all RMV requirements in part 195.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Devices installed under §195.452 for HCAs are subject to the same performance, monitoring, and operational requirements as RMVs elsewhere in part 195.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of risk analyses for certain new/replaced pipelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk analyses and assessments under §195.452 must be completed prior to placing into service all onshore pipelines with diameters of 6 inches or greater that are constructed or that have had 2 or more miles replaced within 5 contiguous miles within a 24‑month period after April 10, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These analyses inform whether emergency flow restricting devices/RMVs are required and ensure findings are implemented per §195.418 before service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for RMV/alternative operations and post‑incident analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators are required to document certain procedures and maintain records pertaining to various aspects of their RMV and alternative equivalent technology operations. Operators who have experienced a rupture or RMV shut‑off are required to complete a post‑incident or ‑accident analysis; the summary of this analysis, all documents used to prepare it, and records of lessons learned must be kept for the useful life of the pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must be retained for the life of the pipeline. PHMSA estimates specific burden hours for these activities; operators should ensure accessible, durable record retention systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written rupture identification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must develop written rupture identification procedures to evaluate and identify whether a notification of potential rupture is an actual rupture event or non‑rupture event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, the procedures must specify the sources of information, operational factors, and other criteria that operator personnel use to evaluate a notification of potential rupture (see §192.635 indicia). Procedures should enable timely, accurate determination to meet closure timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and technical/safety evaluation for alternative equivalent technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators who elect to use alternative equivalent technology must notify PHMSA at least 90 days in advance of use (per §192.18/§195.258) and include a technical and safety evaluation (including design, construction, and operating procedures) with the notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHMSA has 90 days to object by letter; absent objection, the alternative is acceptable after 91 days. For manual valves used as alternatives, the notification must also demonstrate that installation of an RMV would be economically, technically, or operationally infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification triggers and required content (operational failures/exemptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must notify PHMSA for specified circumstances: if an RMV cannot be made operational within 14 days of installation; if a valve cannot be repaired or replaced within 12 months; and when seeking exemptions (e.g., leaving an RMV open >30 minutes if closing would be detrimental to public safety, or requesting increased maximum valve spacing by demonstrating infeasibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHMSA expects roughly 10 percent of operators to make many such notifications; notifications generally require demonstration that compliance is economically, technically, or operationally infeasible per §192.18/§195.18 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve installation requirement for new and entirely replaced segments (≥6 in.)
rubrics_metrics.description: For onshore transmission pipeline segments with diameters ≥6 inches constructed after April 10, 2023, or entirely replaced segments as defined, the operator must install RMVs or an alternative equivalent technology whenever a valve must be installed to meet the applicable valve spacing requirements. Operators seeking to use alternative equivalent technology must notify PHMSA and ensure all RMVs/alternatives meet §§192.634 and 192.636.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions: pipe segments in Class 1, or Class 2 locations with a potential impact radius (PIR) of 150 feet or less are exempt. Operators may request an extension of installation compliance deadlines if they can demonstrate infeasibility via §192.18 notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHMSA review timeline for 'other technology' notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an operator submits a notification under §192.8/§192.9/§192.179/etc. for use of a different integrity assessment method, analytical method, sampling approach, or 'other technology' than prescribed, that notification must be submitted at least 90 days in advance. The operator may proceed 91 days after submission unless PHMSA objects or requires more time/information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 90‑day review regime applies broadly to alternative methods/technologies and is the procedural mechanism for PHMSA to accept, object to, or request further info on proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Added definitions that affect applicability and interpretation: 'entirely replaced onshore transmission pipeline segments' (2+ miles replaced within any 5 contiguous miles within 24 months), 'notification of potential rupture' (notification/observation of indicia identified in §192.635), and 'rupture‑mitigation valve' (RMV defined as ASV or RCV used to minimize volume released and mitigate rupture consequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine which segments and events the RMV and notification requirements apply to; operators should apply definitions when assessing applicability to their assets.
